ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the upper end of resistor R is connected to the power supply terminal labeled +12V; the lower end of R is connected to a common node. This common node is also connected through three ideal diode branches respectively to the 0V reference potential on the left, the 6V reference potential at the lower left, and the 3V reference potential on the right. Then reason: R will pull the common node toward the +12V direction. According to the diode connection directions in the figure, the diode D1 connected to 0V will first become forward-conducting; when an ideal diode conducts, the voltage drop is 0, therefore the common node is clamped at 0V. At this time, the diodes connected to the 3V and 6V reference points are reverse-biased and do not change the potential of this node. Therefore the voltage across resistor R is the upper-end potential minus the lower-end potential: 12V - 0V = 12V.

raw_record.question_text: In the circuit shown in the figure, assuming all diodes are ideal components, what is the voltage across resistor \(R\)?

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the top of R is connected to +12 V, and the bottom node of R is connected to three diode branches leading to 0 V, 6 V, and 3 V. Assume the bottom node is pulled upward by R; the diode to the 0 V reference becomes forward biased first and, being ideal, shorts the bottom node to 0 V. With that node at 0 V, the diodes connected to the 3 V and 6 V references are reverse biased and do not affect the node. Therefore the voltage across R is the difference between its top and bottom terminals: 12 V - 0 V = 12 V.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the straightforward diode-clamp route and is likely the only genuinely distinct solution path for this circuit: determine which ideal diode turns on under the +12 V pull-up, then compute the resistor drop.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram as a +12 V source feeding the top of resistor R, with the lower end of R tied to a junction connected through ideal diodes to 0 V, 6 V, and 3 V reference nodes. From the diode symbols, identify the 0 V branch diode as oriented to conduct from the junction toward the 0 V reference, while the other branches are not forward-biased once the junction is clamped at 0 V.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question statement to apply the assumption that all diodes are ideal and to identify the requested quantity as the voltage across resistor R.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the ideal diode rule: a forward-biased ideal diode is a short circuit with zero voltage drop, and a reverse-biased ideal diode is an open circuit. A pull-up resistor feeding diode clamps will force the junction to the lowest reference voltage accessible through a forward-biased clamp diode.
